### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.pick

### Question

I am wondering how a simple workspace based workflow can be implemented using mini.pick (maybe with mini.extra also). For example, in sublime text and lite-xl, you can add a folder to the project/workspace and then your fuzzy finders automatically include the files for searching. This does not require any LSP whatsoever, it's just a workspace based find_files or live_grep.

A typical workflow when starting a new project is to add the language standard library directories to the workspace so you can easily search for both a function or class in your project as well as in the core libraries.

The core libraries will always reside in the same directory so I don't mind hardcoding the search paths. I just need them to be included in my pickers so I can search them when needed.

comment_data.body:
Not sure the full "file files inside all of these directories" is concisely feasible. Both "find files" and "grep" pickers are mostly designed to work within a single directory. The 'grep_live' picker can take [`globs` argument](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/782969a40d2870b1d7cd7c9db8f965d8aa9705ef/doc/mini-pick.txt#L1100-L1103) to limit the search, but it would have to be filtering paths inside *some* single parent directory.

I think the most realistic approach here would be something like #1141, i.e. a "two staged" search: first select a directory to run search or open file explorer; then do the search or explore. [I use it in my config](https://github.com/echasnovski/nvim/blob/7298d49783c475aca44b8ad68a581681a9171566/plugin/20_mini.lua#L241-L247). For the case of different hardcoded libraries, the first step might be a plain `MiniPick.start()` with custom array of hardcoded paths as items with a similar second step.

reply_data.body:
Thanks for the info, the snippet below works.

```Lua
MiniPick.registry.projects = function()
  local cwd = vim.fn.expand('~/stdlib')
  local choose = function(item)
    vim.schedule(function() MiniPick.builtin.files(nil, { source = { cwd = item.path } }) end)
  end
  return MiniExtra.pickers.explorer({ cwd = cwd }, { source = { choose = choose } })
end
```

This allows me to pick between different directories under '~/stdlib' then launch a files picker after for that directory.

question: if I replace the return statement with the following, I end up in my current directory, why is that? I copied your version out of curiosity.

 ```Lua
 return MiniPick.builtin.files({ cwd = cwd }, { source = { choose = choose } })
```

I am guessing that explorer works only directories but the file picker handles only files.

reply_data.body:
> question: if I replace the return statement with the following, I end up in my current directory, why is that? I copied your version out of curiosity.
> 
> ```lua
> return MiniPick.builtin.files({ cwd = cwd }, { source = { choose = choose } })
> ```
> 
> I am guessing that explorer works only directories but the file picker handles only files.

Not quite. The reason is that [`MiniExtra.pickers.explorer()` supports `cwd` as *local option*](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/782969a40d2870b1d7cd7c9db8f965d8aa9705ef/doc/mini-extra.txt#L310-L311) (because it fits the idea of "explore in *this* directory") while [`MiniPick.builtin.files()` does not](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/782969a40d2870b1d7cd7c9db8f965d8aa9705ef/doc/mini-pick.txt#L1074-L1077). I myself don't really like the inconsistency, but the reason is that `cwd` is the general property of [any picker source](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/782969a40d2870b1d7cd7c9db8f965d8aa9705ef/doc/mini-pick.txt#L297-L306) and having two ways of doing the same thing is a bit redundant.

The [usage in my config](https://github.com/echasnovski/nvim/blob/7298d49783c475aca44b8ad68a581681a9171566/plugin/20_mini.lua#L246) is a mistake that was propagated during my recent config cleanup. It was meant to use `MiniExtra.pickers.explorer` indeed. Sorry for the confusion.

As a workaround, users can [adjust `MiniPick.registry.files`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/782969a40d2870b1d7cd7c9db8f965d8aa9705ef/doc/mini-pick.txt#L1219-L1224) to accept `cwd` as local option. But that would indeed search all *files* in the `cwd` (which can take a bit longer), but maybe that is what you want in the first place. With adjusted registry, you can use `return MiniPick.registry.files({ cwd = cwd }, { source = { choose = choose } })`.
